sources.citation: Prag, Jonathan R. W. 2020. The indigenous languages of Sicily (Las lenguas indigenas de Sicilia). Palaeohispanica. Revista sobre lenguas y culturas de la Hispania Antigua 20 (Palaeoeuropean languages and epigraphies), 531-551. Zaragoza: Institucion Fernando el Catolico. DOI 10.36707/palaeohispanica.v0i20.376.
sources.note: Nothing on prosody; p. 533: 'there is no basis, beyond the already mentioned literary tradition, to identify anything that survives as evidence for a Sikan language, distinct from Sikel' -- i.e. no analysable Sikan corpus, hence no phonology.

sources.citation: PRIN 2017 'Lingue e culture dell'Italia antica: linguistica storica e modelli digitali' (Universita di Firenze, coord.). Project web page 'Le lingue anelleniche della Sicilia', prin-italia-antica.unifi.it, accessed 2026-09-21.
sources.note: No phonology content for Sicanian: the page summarises the corpus (4-6 uninterpreted fragmentary texts) and gives a 7-item bibliography (Agostiniani 1977, Biondi 1995, De Simone 1999, Prosdocimi 1998, Poccetti 2012, Marchesini 2012, Prag 2020), all either about Elymian/Sicel or already held by the project. Nothing on accent, stress or tone.

sources.citation: Tribulato, Olga. 2015. Interferenza grafemica ed interferenza linguistica nella Sicilia antica. In: Contatti di lingue - Contatti di scritture: Multilinguismo e multigrafismo dal Vicino Oriente Antico alla Cina contemporanea (Filologie medievali e moderne 9), 59-83. Venezia: Edizioni Ca' Foscari. DOI 10.14277/978-88-6969/FMM-9-2.
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone. Content is graphemic (Greek alphabet of Gela type at Montagna di Marzo, 'alpha siculum', phonetic value of the 'reversed N' and beta in Elymian area) and morphological (dative endings). Confirms there is no separately describable Sicanian sound system.

sources.citation: Agostiniani, Luciano. 2012. Alfabetizzazione della Sicilia pregreca. Aristonothos: Scritti per il Mediterraneo antico 4 (Convivenze etniche e contatti di culture), 139-164. Milano. DOI 10.6092/2037-4488/1940.
sources.note: No phonology of Sicanian at all: the paper is about alphabet adoption (Elymian and Sicel scripts, 'alpha siculum', letter values). Its decisive content for this languoid is negative: there is no Sicanian corpus; the only phonological remarks (fricatives, missing phonemes) concern Elymian/Sicel grapheme values. Word stress/tone unrecoverable in principle.
